intro.title: Discover Fontaine Saint-Michel
intro.notice: Note: Currently due to partial repair or maintenance, there may be enclosures. Please confirm the latest open status before visiting.
intro.description:
Standing proudly at the intersection of Boulevard Saint-Michel and Place Saint-Michel, the Fontaine Saint-Michel is one of Paris's most recognizable monuments. Built between 1858 and 1860 under the direction of architect Gabriel Davioud during Baron Haussmann's massive urban renovation of Paris.

The fountain's centerpiece is the impressive statue of Archangel Michael defeating the devil, created by sculptor Francisque Jouffroy. The monumental structure rises 26 meters high and features four Corinthian columns framing the central niche, with two allegorical figures representing Law and Justice on either side.

Located in the heart of the Latin Quarter, the fountain has served as a popular meeting point for Parisians and tourists alike for over 160 years. Its strategic position connects the Left Bank's vibrant student district with the historic Île de la Cité, making it an essential landmark in Paris's cultural landscape.

The fountain is beautifully illuminated at night, creating a magical atmosphere in the bustling Place Saint-Michel. It's freely accessible 24/7, making it perfect for both daytime exploration and evening strolls through Paris's enchanting streets.

sections.title: History & Construction
sections.content:
The Fontaine Saint-Michel was commissioned as part of Baron Haussmann's massive urban renovation project in 19th-century Paris. Architect Gabriel Davioud designed this monumental fountain between 1858 and 1860, creating what would become one of the most iconic public monuments in the Latin Quarter.

The fountain was strategically placed at the entrance to Rue Danton, marking the boundary between the bustling commercial district and the historic Latin Quarter. Its construction represented the Second Empire's commitment to beautifying Paris with grand public works that combined artistic excellence with functional urban design.

sections.title: Architectural Significance
sections.content:
Standing 26 meters tall, the Fontaine Saint-Michel is a masterpiece of Second Empire architecture. The structure features four majestic Corinthian columns that frame the central niche. The red marble columns contrast beautifully with the white stone facade, creating a striking visual impact.

The central niche houses the dramatic group sculpture of Archangel Michael vanquishing the devil, carved by Francisque Jouffroy. Two allegorical figures adorn the sides: 'Law' by Louis-Auguste Barrias on the left, and 'Justice' by Alexandre Falguière on the right. The fountain's basin collects water from four spouts shaped like marine monsters.

sections.title: The Latin Quarter Setting
sections.content:
Place Saint-Michel has been a vibrant crossroads since ancient times. During the Roman era, this area marked the boundary between the Île de la Cité and the Left Bank. The fountain's location at the junction of Boulevard Saint-Michel and Quai Saint-Michel makes it a natural gathering point.

The surrounding area is filled with historic cafés, bookshops, and the Sorbonne University. The fountain has witnessed countless student protests, romantic meetings, and tourist encounters. It's also the starting point for the famous Boulevard Saint-Michel, which stretches all the way to the Luxembourg Gardens.

sections.title: Cultural Impact
sections.content:
Fontaine Saint-Michel has appeared in numerous films, photographs, and works of literature. It serves as a symbol of the Latin Quarter's bohemian spirit and intellectual heritage. The fountain is particularly beloved by students from the nearby Sorbonne, who have adopted it as an unofficial meeting spot.

During the 1968 student protests, the fountain area was a focal point of activity. Today, it remains a popular meeting place, with locals often saying 'Let's meet at Saint-Michel' — referring to the fountain. The monument's enduring appeal lies in its perfect integration into Paris's urban fabric, serving both as art and as a functional part of city life.

tickets.title: Ticket Information
tickets.infoDesc: As a public monument, Fontaine Saint-Michel is freely accessible. No guided tours are offered on-site. For more information about the fountain's history and architecture, please refer to official Paris tourism resources.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take RER B direct to 'Saint-Michel Notre-Dame' station (approx. 45 min, €11.80). The fountain is right outside the station.
transport.fromOrlyDesc: Take Orlyval + RER B to 'Saint-Michel Notre-Dame' station (approx. 60 min, €14.10). The fountain is right outside the station.
transport.fromCenterDesc: Walk 5 minutes from Notre-Dame across Petit Pont to Boulevard Saint-Michel. The fountain is impossible to miss at the intersection.
transport.fromStationDesc: The station is right next to the fountain. Served by RER B, RER C, and Metro Line 10. Exit following 'Sortie Place Saint-Michel' signs.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Metro Line 10 to 'Cluny - La Sorbonne' (3 min walk) or 'Odéon' (5 min walk). RER B/C to 'Saint-Michel Notre-Dame' (direct access).
transport.walkingDesc: Perfect starting point for Latin Quarter exploration — walk to Sorbonne (3 min), Shakespeare & Company (5 min), Panthéon (10 min).
transport.drivingDesc: Limited parking in area. Recommended to use public transport. The area is pedestrian-friendly with many attractions within walking distance.

route.title: Recommended Walking Route
route.overview: Start at Fontaine Saint-Michel, walk to Shakespeare & Company (5 min), continue to Notre-Dame (5 min), cross to Île de la Cité, visit Sainte-Chapelle (10 min), then explore Latin Quarter's narrow streets and end at Luxembourg Gardens (15 min). Total walking time: about 2-3 hours including breaks.
steps: Start at Fontaine Saint-Michel, admire the 26m tall monumental structure
Walk along Boulevard Saint-Michel to Shakespeare & Company bookstore (5 minutes)
Browse the famous English-language bookstore, soak in literary atmosphere
Continue to Notre-Dame Cathedral via Petit Pont (5 minutes)
Admire Notre-Dame's facade (exterior view due to reconstruction)
Cross back to Left Bank, walk along Quai de Montebello
Visit Sainte-Chapelle on Île de la Cité (10 minutes from Notre-Dame)
Return to Latin Quarter, explore Rue de la Huchette
Stop at a traditional café on Place de la Sorbonne
End at Luxembourg Gardens, relax and enjoy the scenery

officialManagement.title: About Fontaine Saint-Michel
officialManagement.text:
The Fontaine Saint-Michel is a monumental public fountain located in Place Saint-Michel, 5th arrondissement of Paris. Built between 1858 and 1860 by architect Gabriel Davioud, it stands as one of the most iconic monuments of the Latin Quarter.

The fountain features a dramatic sculpture of Archangel Michael defeating the devil, flanked by allegorical figures of Law and Justice. At 26 meters tall with its distinctive Corinthian columns, it has been a beloved meeting point and photographic subject for over 160 years.
